_readme: Hand-curated, not archive-mined. The civic/justice cluster from the conversation 'Fractal reasoning across civic and justice narratives' (2026-09-09), added by plans/civic-structures-and-loops.md Stage 2. Films and series here are MEDIUMS, not entities: they carry the testimony of the institutions, families, cities and groups listed under civicEntities, which are the things that actually maintain a boundary against their own dissolution (fractal_operational_core.md section 1). A policy is NOT an entity either — it is a posture an institution holds, so it lives in that institution's `postures` array with a date and a falsifier, never as a row of its own.

cluster.name: Civic Structures, Justice & the Shadow of the Law

grounding.note: Written by hand from the works themselves, 2026-09-09. Not archive-mined; provenance is the work named in each entity's testimony list.

f_fences.title: Fences
f_fences.synopsis: A Pittsburgh sanitation worker, barred from organised baseball by the colour line, rebuilds that same boundary inside his own yard.

f_when_they_see_us.title: When They See Us
f_when_they_see_us.synopsis: Five Harlem teenagers are coerced into confessions after a Central Park assault, convicted, and exonerated years later.

f_the_wire.title: The Wire
f_the_wire.synopsis: One Baltimore pattern read at five rungs — the corner, the docks, city hall, the schools, the paper — each institution surviving at the expense of the people it claims to serve.

f_the_corner.title: The Corner
f_the_corner.synopsis: A year on one West Baltimore corner, told through a family the drug trade is dismantling from the inside.

f_show_me_a_hero.title: Show Me a Hero
f_show_me_a_hero.synopsis: A federal desegregation order lands on Yonkers, and the city survives its own deadlock by consuming the young mayor who has to enforce it.

f_city_of_god.title: City of God
f_city_of_god.synopsis: A housing project built at Rio's edge and left without a single civic membrane; the children inside organise the only order available to them.

f_precious.title: Precious
f_precious.synopsis: An illiterate, abused Harlem teenager carries a household's whole weight, invisible to the school and the welfare office until an alternative school makes a place for her to exist.

f_beasts_of_no_nation.title: Beasts of No Nation
f_beasts_of_no_nation.synopsis: A militia offers a boy shelter and brotherhood after his family is killed, and within weeks the shelter is the machine that makes him a killer.

f_say_nothing.title: Say Nothing
f_say_nothing.synopsis: The Troubles read through one disappearance and the fighters the movement silenced once peace made them an embarrassment.

f_i_know_this_much_is_true.title: I Know This Much Is True
f_i_know_this_much_is_true.synopsis: Twin brothers, one schizophrenic, and a family whose inherited silence is administered by a forensic hospital.

f_zero_dark_thirty.title: Zero Dark Thirty
f_zero_dark_thirty.synopsis: A decade-long manhunt in which an agency's need for a body to produce reorganises everything, including the people running it.

characters.name: Troy Maxson
characters.note: Kept out of organised baseball by the colour line and shaped by a penitentiary youth, he draws the same boundary around his own family — and the fence that was built to keep the world out ends up exiling his son.
characters.synopsis: A Pittsburgh sanitation worker, barred from organised baseball by the colour line, rebuilds that same boundary inside his own yard.

characters.name: Rose Maxson
characters.note: Holds the household together by absorbing what the men will not carry; her forgiveness at the end is a decision taken in full sight of the cost, not a feeling.
characters.synopsis: A Pittsburgh sanitation worker, barred from organised baseball by the colour line, rebuilds that same boundary inside his own yard.

characters.name: Cory Maxson
characters.note: The son the fence was built to protect, and then to keep out; he inherits the refusal along with the house.
characters.synopsis: A Pittsburgh sanitation worker, barred from organised baseball by the colour line, rebuilds that same boundary inside his own yard.

characters.name: Gabriel Maxson
characters.note: A head wound from the war bought the house his brother lives in; when his presence turns into an administrative nuisance, the signature that commits him is his brother's.
characters.synopsis: A Pittsburgh sanitation worker, barred from organised baseball by the colour line, rebuilds that same boundary inside his own yard.

characters.name: Korey Wise
characters.note: Went to the precinct to keep a friend company, was the only one tried as an adult, and served the longest — his psyche fractured into survival states to endure solitary confinement.
characters.synopsis: Five Harlem teenagers are coerced into confessions after a Central Park assault, convicted, and exonerated years later.

characters.name: Antron McCray
characters.note: Fourteen, kept awake thirty hours, and told by his own father to sign — the father's nerve broken by the room before the son's was.
characters.synopsis: Five Harlem teenagers are coerced into confessions after a Central Park assault, convicted, and exonerated years later.

characters.name: Bobby McCray
characters.note: Under thirty hours of institutional pressure he tells his son to sign what they want; he is structurally unable to transmit protection because the state has taught him there is none.
characters.synopsis: Five Harlem teenagers are coerced into confessions after a Central Park assault, convicted, and exonerated years later.

characters.name: Yusef Salaam
characters.note: Refused to sign, was convicted anyway, and carried the branding through his whole adolescence before the record was vacated.
characters.synopsis: Five Harlem teenagers are coerced into confessions after a Central Park assault, convicted, and exonerated years later.

characters.name: D'Angelo Barksdale
characters.note: The nephew who can see the shape of the thing he is inside and cannot get out of it; the family's business is also the family's boundary.
characters.synopsis: One Baltimore pattern read at five rungs — the corner, the docks, city hall, the schools, the paper — each institution surviving at the expense of the people it claims to serve.

characters.name: Howard 'Bunny' Colvin
characters.note: Tired of watching the drug war destroy the district it claims to protect, he draws a perimeter instead of making arrests — a containment answer his own institution cannot tolerate.
characters.synopsis: One Baltimore pattern read at five rungs — the corner, the docks, city hall, the schools, the paper — each institution surviving at the expense of the people it claims to serve.

characters.name: Stringer Bell
characters.note: Runs the corner like a firm and discovers the two logics are the same one, and that neither will admit him.
characters.synopsis: One Baltimore pattern read at five rungs — the corner, the docks, city hall, the schools, the paper — each institution surviving at the expense of the people it claims to serve.

characters.name: Jimmy McNulty
characters.note: Right about the case and wrong about everything else; his need to be the one who sees it is the department's pathology at individual scale.
characters.synopsis: One Baltimore pattern read at five rungs — the corner, the docks, city hall, the schools, the paper — each institution surviving at the expense of the people it claims to serve.

characters.name: Omar Little
characters.note: Lives outside every code but his own and is legible to no institution — which is exactly why the street's rules bend around him until they don't.
characters.synopsis: One Baltimore pattern read at five rungs — the corner, the docks, city hall, the schools, the paper — each institution surviving at the expense of the people it claims to serve.

characters.name: Gary McCullough
characters.note: Was the one who made it out and came back in; his gentleness is the part of him the corner has no use for.
characters.synopsis: A year on one West Baltimore corner, told through a family the drug trade is dismantling from the inside.

characters.name: Fran Boyd
characters.note: Runs a household and an addiction at once, and the recovery, when it comes, is a boundary she has to draw against people she loves.
characters.synopsis: A year on one West Baltimore corner, told through a family the drug trade is dismantling from the inside.

characters.name: DeAndre McCullough
characters.note: Fifteen, already holding a package, already reading the arrest as the fee rather than the risk.
characters.synopsis: A year on one West Baltimore corner, told through a family the drug trade is dismantling from the inside.

characters.name: Nick Wasicsko
characters.note: The young mayor who has to enforce a desegregation order nobody with more power will own; the city survives its deadlock by consuming him.
characters.synopsis: A federal desegregation order lands on Yonkers, and the city survives its own deadlock by consuming the young mayor who has to enforce it.

characters.name: Mary Dorman
characters.note: Opposes the housing until she meets the people who will live in it, and then has to carry the reversal in public.
characters.synopsis: A federal desegregation order lands on Yonkers, and the city survives its own deadlock by consuming the young mayor who has to enforce it.

characters.name: Rocket
characters.note: Survives by becoming an eye — a photographer who documents the violence without touching it, which is both his escape and his compromise.
characters.synopsis: A housing project built at Rio's edge and left without a single civic membrane; the children inside organise the only order available to them.

characters.name: Lil Zé
characters.note: Metabolises an absolute lack of worth into unrestrained sovereignty; the vacuum the state left is the shape he grows into.
characters.synopsis: A housing project built at Rio's edge and left without a single civic membrane; the children inside organise the only order available to them.

characters.name: Knockout Ned
characters.note: Pulled into the war by a private wrong and discovers that the war has no private register — every act is immediately collective.
characters.synopsis: A housing project built at Rio's edge and left without a single civic membrane; the children inside organise the only order available to them.

characters.name: Claireece 'Precious' Jones
characters.note: Carries a household's whole multi-generational weight and is invisible to both the school and the welfare office until an alternative school makes a place for her to exist.
characters.synopsis: An illiterate, abused Harlem teenager carries a household's whole weight, invisible to the school and the welfare office until an alternative school makes a place for her to exist.

characters.name: Mary Lee Johnston
characters.note: Both the instrument of the consumption and a person consumed; the welfare interview is the one place the whole arrangement is spoken aloud.
characters.synopsis: An illiterate, abused Harlem teenager carries a household's whole weight, invisible to the school and the welfare office until an alternative school makes a place for her to exist.

characters.name: Ms. Rain
characters.note: Teaches in the alternative school — the buffering membrane the main system could not supply, staffed by someone who stays inside the tissue.
characters.synopsis: An illiterate, abused Harlem teenager carries a household's whole weight, invisible to the school and the welfare office until an alternative school makes a place for her to exist.

characters.name: Agu
characters.note: A boy whose family is killed by government troops and who is taken in by the militia that then makes him do the same thing; the shelter and the slaughterhouse are one building.
characters.synopsis: A militia offers a boy shelter and brotherhood after his family is killed, and within weeks the shelter is the machine that makes him a killer.

characters.name: The Commandant
characters.note: Offers vengeance and brotherhood to children with nothing left, and the offer is real — which is what makes it work.
characters.synopsis: A militia offers a boy shelter and brotherhood after his family is killed, and within weeks the shelter is the machine that makes him a killer.

characters.name: Dolours Price
characters.note: Carried out the movement's orders, spent decades holding what she did, and at the end recorded her confession for an archive because no living body would receive it.
characters.synopsis: The Troubles read through one disappearance and the fighters the movement silenced once peace made them an embarrassment.

characters.name: Brendan Hughes
characters.note: The commander the movement needed and then could not acknowledge; his testimony had to wait for his death to be released.
characters.synopsis: The Troubles read through one disappearance and the fighters the movement silenced once peace made them an embarrassment.

characters.name: Jean McConville
characters.note: A widowed mother of ten taken from her flat and disappeared; the community that took her then had to keep the silence that took her.
characters.synopsis: The Troubles read through one disappearance and the fighters the movement silenced once peace made them an embarrassment.

characters.name: Dominick Birdsey
characters.filmTitle: I Know This Much Is True
characters.note: Spends his life as his brother's only advocate against a forensic system that has no slot for advocacy, and inherits the family's silence as a job.
characters.synopsis: Twin brothers, one schizophrenic, and a family whose inherited silence is administered by a forensic hospital.

characters.name: Thomas Birdsey
characters.filmTitle: I Know This Much Is True
characters.note: His illness is legible to the hospital only as risk; the act that puts him inside is a religious one the intake form has no field for.
characters.synopsis: Twin brothers, one schizophrenic, and a family whose inherited silence is administered by a forensic hospital.

characters.name: Maya
characters.note: Becomes the agency's certainty in a single body; when the body is finally produced there is nothing left of her that was not the hunt.
characters.synopsis: A decade-long manhunt in which an agency's need for a body to produce reorganises everything, including the people running it.

characters.name: Dan
characters.note: Runs the interrogations and then leaves the room for a desk, carrying the method out with him rather than answering for it.
characters.synopsis: A decade-long manhunt in which an agency's need for a body to produce reorganises everything, including the people running it.

civicEntities.name: Pittsburgh
civicEntities.note: The Hill District in the late 1950s: a city whose promise of opportunity was administered as a grammar of exclusion written into who gets the loan, the promotion, the truck.

civicEntities.name: New York City
civicEntities.note: A civic body that suffers an acute rupture, cannot metabolise its own fear, and reaches into Harlem for five bodies to close the edge with.

civicEntities.name: Baltimore
civicEntities.note: One pattern read at five rungs — the corner, the docks, city hall, the schools, the paper — each institution optimising for its own survival at the expense of the people it exists to serve.

civicEntities.name: Yonkers
civicEntities.note: A city ordered by a federal court to desegregate its public housing, which answers by pushing the whole political cost onto one office.

civicEntities.name: Rio de Janeiro
civicEntities.note: Pushes its poor to the barren periphery to keep the tourist zone legible to itself, then supplies the periphery with no schools, no clinics and no courts.

civicEntities.name: Belfast
civicEntities.note: A city where the civic structure of resistance became its own machinery of exile, and where the peace was built on sealed archives rather than public confession.

civicEntities.name: Pittsburgh Sanitation Department
civicEntities.note: The crew Troy Maxson lifts for: Black men on the back of the truck, white men behind the wheel, a rule nobody had to write down until somebody asked why.

postures.name: Only white men drive the trucks
postures.source: Fences (August Wilson, 1985) — Troy's grievance to the union, Act One
postures.falsifier: A Black driver on the Pittsburgh sanitation rolls before 1957 would break this reading of the posture's duration.

civicEntities.name: Organised baseball's colour line
civicEntities.note: The rule that kept Troy out of the majors in his prime and then, when it fell, kept him out again by being too late — an exclusion whose repeal does not return the years.

postures.name: No Black players in the major leagues
postures.source: Fences (August Wilson, 1985); the historical colour bar in organised baseball
postures.falsifier: A Black player on a major-league roster between 1889 and 1947 would break the stated span.

civicEntities.name: NYPD Manhattan North homicide/sex-crimes detectives
civicEntities.note: The interrogation rooms where the city's unmanageable panic was pressed into five adolescent bodies until they signed.

postures.name: Question juveniles at length without a guardian present
postures.source: When They See Us (2019); the vacated convictions in the Central Park jogger case, 2002
postures.falsifier: A contemporaneous departmental rule requiring a guardian, and evidence it was followed here, would break this.

civicEntities.name: Manhattan District Attorney's sex crimes unit
civicEntities.note: The office that carried the case to trial on the confessions and against the physical evidence, and whose theory the city needed to be true.

postures.name: Prosecute on the confessions despite unmatched DNA
postures.source: When They See Us (2019); the 2002 reinvestigation and vacatur
postures.falsifier: Contemporaneous DNA linking any of the five to the scene would break this.

civicEntities.name: Baltimore Police Department
civicEntities.note: A patrol system that cannot reliably tell the tissue it protects from the thing it hunts, and that escalates as the scar tissue thickens.

postures.name: CompStat — the district is measured by its arrest tally
postures.falsifier: A district evaluated on clearance quality rather than arrest count, in the same period, would break this.

postures.name: Hamsterdam — a tolerated free zone that buffers rather than exterminates
postures.falsifier: The zone surviving the political reaction would break the reading that the institution could not tolerate it.

civicEntities.name: The Barksdale organisation
civicEntities.note: A firm with the same liquidation logic as any other: liability held by the youngest bodies, revenue by the oldest.

civicEntities.name: Baltimore City Public Schools
civicEntities.note: The intake interface for every child the corner is about to recruit, and the rung where the loop is least defended.

civicEntities.name: The Baltimore Sun
civicEntities.note: The organ that was supposed to make the city legible to itself, cutting the reporters who knew the ground while chasing the prize story.

civicEntities.name: Yonkers City Council
civicEntities.note: Could not bear to tell its constituents the law must be obeyed, nor bear the contempt fines, so it shifted the whole load onto one young mayor.

postures.name: Refuse the federal desegregation order
postures.source: Show Me a Hero (2015); United States v. Yonkers Board of Education
postures.falsifier: Compliance before the contempt fines began would break the stated span.

civicEntities.name: Rio military police
civicEntities.note: Enters the project as an occupying force and leaves as a supplier; the boundary between the patrol and the trade dissolves in both directions.

civicEntities.name: New York City welfare office
civicEntities.note: Means-tests the household and therefore cannot see the child inside it; the interview is the one place the whole arrangement is finally said out loud.

postures.name: Assess the household as the unit, not the child
postures.falsifier: A contemporaneous rule requiring the child be interviewed separately would break this.

civicEntities.name: Each One Teach One alternative school
civicEntities.note: The membrane the main system could not supply: small, inside the tissue, and buffering rather than sorting.

civicEntities.name: The Provisional IRA
civicEntities.note: A civic structure of resistance that becomes its own machinery of exile — first of the woman it disappeared, then of the fighters who became an embarrassment to the peace.

civicEntities.name: HM Prison Maze
civicEntities.note: Where the state held what it would not name, and where the hunger strike turned the prisoner's own body into the last available instrument.

civicEntities.name: Hatch Forensic Institute
civicEntities.note: Reads a religious act as a risk score, because risk is the only field the intake form has.

civicEntities.name: CIA Counterterrorism Center
civicEntities.note: An agency that needs a body to produce, and reorganises its methods, its people and its truth around producing one.

civicEntities.name: Cidade de Deus
civicEntities.note: The housing project itself: an entity the state created by subtraction, holding itself together with the only order its children could build.

civicEntities.name: The Commandant's battalion
civicEntities.note: Nominally a shelter against extermination; within weeks the shelter is the machine that erodes a child's ability to tell love from obedience.

civicEntities.name: The Fayette Street corner
civicEntities.note: A market with a full labour hierarchy, a training programme and a pension of exactly nothing, holding a neighbourhood together the way a wound holds a body together.

civicEntities.name: Troy and Bono's truck crew
civicEntities.note: Two men on the back of the same truck for years. The smallest civic structure in the film, and — the anatomy found — the one whose boundary Troy actually defends: his ally in the household scene is his workmate, not his kin.

civicEntities.name: The Maxson household
civicEntities.note: A civic space with its own laws, its own exiles and its own unspoken constitution: a fortress against the world's violence that becomes the instrument of its own isolation.

civicEntities.name: The McCray family
civicEntities.note: The father's nerve breaks in the interrogation room before the son's does, and the family is dissolved by the signature that was supposed to end the night.

civicEntities.name: The Wise family
civicEntities.note: A mother's faith in the civic covenant collapses into despair, and the collapse travels outward into how a whole block deals with the precinct.

civicEntities.name: The Barksdale family
civicEntities.note: Where the firm and the kinship are the same structure, so leaving the business and leaving the family are one act.

civicEntities.name: The McCullough/Boyd family
civicEntities.note: Three generations on one corner, each of them at a different point in the same loop at the same time.

civicEntities.name: The Jones/Johnston household
civicEntities.note: A sealed room in which a multi-generational weight is transmitted downward and the outside world's two institutions are trained not to look in.

civicEntities.name: The McConville family
civicEntities.note: Ten children left in a flat after their mother is taken, then dispersed into institutions — the disappearance administered twice.

civicEntities.name: The Price family
civicEntities.note: A republican lineage in which the movement is the inheritance, and the daughters carry an obligation that was decided before they existed.

civicEntities.name: The Birdsey family
civicEntities.note: A household organised around a silence about paternity, which the next generation administers on the family's behalf without ever being told what it is.
